complaint_text: LG Refrigerator I removed the bottom glass shelve from the refrigerator because we had spilled something on it. I placed it in the kitchen sink and washed both sides with dishwasher soap and a sponge. Then I rinsed it off with warn/hot water. All of a sudden the glass shelve exploded into many tiny pieces. I received superficial cuts to my hand and arm. I immediately called LG to report it and they sent me a replacement glass shelve. I reviewed the use and care manual and nowhere did it mention not to remove the ice cold shelves from the refrigeration and wash them with hot water. I am reporting this because I would hate to see what might have happened if a young child was standing next to me. I believe the glass shelve they are using is not tempered. Therefore creating a potential hazard.

My house at [REDACTED] had a Rinnai Tankless Water Heater installed several years ago. On December 15, 2025, I came back from doing a morning chore, while 5 friends and family members were in the house doing morning routine including showering, and as I pulled into the garage, heavy smoke and very strong burning smell filled the garage. Everyone stopped what they were doing and rushed out to the garage. It took us sometime to figure out, that the smoke came from the Rinnai tankless water heater. The garage dry wall around the heater's air vent has turned black. As gas line was right there, had we discovered the smoke minutes later, it could have caused a major fire or gas explosion, and it could have endangered people's lives and burned down my house. I called [REDACTED] in Las Vegas who installed the product and reported the incident. They said it was between us and Rinnai. Rinnai refused to accept calls from us. Their online chat refused to discuss the case with me. Rinnai only talk to licensed contractors. They demanded that I pay for a licensed electrician to come on site to perform certain testing to prove to them that the fire is cause by external electrical wiring. I hired a brand new electrical company who is fully licensed and spoke with Rinnai on the phone. After the live testing on the phone with Rinnai's tech department, the electrician concluded that the fire was caused by Rinnai's internal circuit board, not faulty wiring external to the heater. I believe Rinnai has a faulty product that is threatening the safety of the public, potentially life threatening, and can cause serious damages to properties. Rinnai's attitude toward the handling of this incident is appalling. They first gave a conditional approval to [REDACTED] who was essentially price gauging me with a $2850 bill for reinstalling a product that is less than $2000. Then Rinnai revoked the free replacement when a second company, Johny On The Spot came, and who tried everything they can to fin

I purchased a Samsung 3-door Refrigerator in April 2020. The unit was within normal working parameters until April 2022. I began noticing ice build up in the vents at the back of the refrigerator section. This build-up did not affect any part or operation of the unit at this time. At the end of April 2022, I noticed my deli drawer at the bottom of the unit was stuck, it wouldn't move. Thanks to a layer of ice that formed, the drawer was going nowhere. I also noticed that food was going bad quicker than it normally would. The temperature from the top shelf reported 55F when the panel read 37F. Each week, I would remove the deli drawer and break out the layer of ice that had accumulated before drying it out. At the end of May 2022, food stored in the unit began to spoil within days of purchasing. A gallon of milk had spoiled within a day. In June of 2022, I had my first repair bill for it for $350. Samsung had scheduled the repair from a company on their authorized lists. Upon arrival, the repair person knew within moments of the issue, as they described this situation as the most common one they face: a faulty temperature sensor. This sensor messages the coolant system telling it if the fridge needs colder or to stand down. This fluctuation from the sensor's failure caused ice build-up that blocks the air vents, which raises the internal temperature. The fix was immediate and had no further issues until March of 2023. The ice build-up was back and I began removing it every two weeks. I reached out to Samsung asking for the repair to a device they replaced less than a year ago, but was told there was no authorized repairfolk in the {REDACTED] area so I would have to schedule my service and then file a claim to see IF the warranty of only the sensor would be covered (but there may be other 'issues' discovered'). At the time, the ice removal was not a huge issue so I did nothing In May of 2023, my food began to spoil within days of purchasing, again. Contacting Samsung,

The unit appeared to have burned from the inside of the unit

I purchased an LG washing machine. When it was delivered on January 3rd, 2023, I noticed some chemical odor but I attributed it to the plastic and styrofoam packaging the machine had been packed in, and I expected it would dissipate now that the machine was unboxed and the packaging was not in my house. I avoided being in the room with it for the first couple of days but I did have exacerbation of asthma symptoms after the washing machine came into my house. On January 5th when the odor was no longer detectable in the room, I hooked up the machine and followed the instructions in the manual to run a test load. I noticed the odor was still there when I opened the machine to put the test load in. After I ran the test load it had not spun properly and the items were sopping wet, plus the odor was now very strong. It smelled something like turpentine. I contacted LG customer support via the chat function on their website. The customer support agent instructed me to run a rinse and spin cycle again. I did that, and this time it did spin, but the chemical odor was still very strong. I told the customer support agent that it smelled a lot like turpentine. The agent asked if it smelled musty or mildewy, and I repeated that it smelled more like turpentine than anything else I could think of. The agent advised me to run a tub clean cycle. I did that, and the odor permeated my house and severely exacerbated my asthma symptoms. The following day I called LG customer support, thinking this was a defective unit and could be exchanged. But this time the customer service agent told me that it is normal for their new machines to emit these fumes, and I should run up to 10 more loads to dissipate it. In the meantime my asthma symptoms escalated until I had to go to an urgent care clinic. I do not think it is reasonable to expect people to run 10 loads on a machine that is emitting fumes which trigger asthma attacks.

KitchenAid Microwave/Hood combination model # KHMS155LSS-3, serial # TRS4039513 purchased installed October 2005 when the building (new structure) was built. I noticed that several times, the microwave seemed to have gone on by itself, because I noticed several time that it said: "END" on the display panel. On two occasions I noticed it go on and it usually lasted anywhere from 30 secs to a minute and sometimes longer. When I noticed this, I immediately unplugged it. I called the building manager who told me that over 20 units have reported the same problem. When the first two or three were reported to KitchenAid they sent a replacement control panel which seems to go awry after a while and charged the owners some $300. When it got more prevalent, the building manager called KitchenAid and spoke to a supervisor who agreed to refund the money and from then on, they have been replacing the control panel for free. I think this could be a real fire hazard especially for unit owners who go on vacation and do not unplug the units. It certainly had a lot to do with an increase of my electrical bill last month. KitchenAid has not offered any explanation for this problem.

I have a recalled Samsung Washer. It's a 700 dollar washer that the extended warranty was still good on when this all started. Was told to wait and see what they would be doing. Now that extended warranty has expired, and their idea of a fix is Dish Network coming out and installing 2 bolts, and stickers going on the machine, changing the bedding cycle to the delicate cycle which in NO WAY spins heavy bulky items enough. Or they offered me 256 dollars towards another Samsung washer or 156 dollars on a non-samsung washer. This is NOT ACCEPTABLE! I have seen several people still have issues after the "fix" The inside of my drum is chewed up from this issues, and I was told I could address that with the repair tech when they came out, only DISH was coming out and said they couldn't do anything. I've seen recalled machines still in the stores. I don't think I should have to suffer because I refuse another of their washers!

The consumer indicates that his washer does not shut off. In order to shut the unit off, the consumer must switch off its breaker. The consumer states that the unit is used thrice per week. The consumer contacted his warranty company and explained the situation; the representative deemed the unit a "lemon" and irreparable. The consumer is planning on keeping his washer for at least the next thirty days in case an investigation ensues.

Caller stated that the refrigerator is defective, the temperature displayed is not the actual temperature in the unit which is a food safety issue. The ice maker does not work properly. She has contacted the company and they have not sent out any service technician for repairs, she has had to use outside repair technicians at her own expense. Caller stated that that she has seen numerous complaints on [REDACTED] about these problem on these refrigerators. She stated that the company is aware of these problems but still continue to make these units. Caller feels that this refrigerator is unsafe and should be reported.

Caller stated that she had used the cleaning feature and when she tried to use the oven for baking after a few mins she heard a loud noise which interrupted her lights and appliances. She had to use the circuit breaker to switch back on the power. Caller feels that her model and serial should be added to the recall 09-333. She does not want her range repaired due to the hazard it poses and would like when she purchase another one to be reimburse in case it becomes a recall. (7/2014)The manufacturer was contacted and she was advised that her model and serial number was not included in the recall. From consent letter: "I believe the oven worked fine until I first used the cleaning feature when the oven was on a very high temperature for an extended period of time. This feature should be tested before marketing this product as I believe it ruined my oven."

A little over a year ago, on November 23, 2010, we replaced our 30+ year old electric tankless, electric water heater, made by the prior owner of your company, with a Bosch Powerstream Pro. I cannot give you the serial number, because it is hidden behind its internal pipes. I cannot see it even crawling under the sink with a flashlight in hand. When the Bosch heater works, it is wonderful, but when it does not work, and I am reduced to heating water on the kitchen stove to wash dishes or hands, it is a curse. And, it is an intermittent curse, the worst kind. When the plumber who installed it comes, it works. When he is gone, it may, or may not work. This device has given me pause about my very long time admiration of German engineering~ (GeI1nan cars from 1961 to and including the present.) This is now the second episode of outages. My prior, American made model always worked during its long lifetime. I find myself grieving over its death and its subsequent replacement with your Bosch. In addition to not being able to read the serial number, which is inside the cover behind piping, etc., one cannot access the restart button without opening the protective cover. When the cover is opened, the inner wiring and piping are exposed, and they surround the restart button, and that is how I received a strong electric shock yesterday, attempting to push the restart button. The danger of your heater has thus been dramatically demonstrated to me. While I hesitate to give someone of your status and expertise advice, it seems obvious, that to protect consumers, both the serial number and the restart button should be placed in a safe and easily accessible location. Since I have wisely switched from trying to push the reset button with my finger, ever hopeful, trying to get it to restart, using instead the wooden handle of a spatula in a move toward self-preservation, I have concluded that the restart button seems not to push. I was burned by a microwave that turned on when it was open. The food didn't finish cooking. The screen said LOC. I pressed the door open button and when the door opened the microwave turned on
Recall

While cooking item wrapped in paper towel in microwave oven, paper towel caught fire. [REDACTED] frozen dinner also caught fire while cooking. Small hole burned in wall of microwave. Also burn marks on side of oven where rack attaches.

I bought my home in Dec 2011, just recently my dishwasher caught on fire. My daughter and I thought something melted on it. There was no sign of any distress on any plates, glasses , etc. We never put plastic in it. On the bottom lid of the dishwasher where the hot iron is, is where the burn marks are on the dishwasher. I heard on the news that there is a recall on these dishwashers but mine is not in it. You can see where and smell the burn smell coming from it. This is without the washer being in use. The brand of my dishwasher is Model Number # GD2200GO2WW Serial # is SG82065B. My house was built in 2006 so it was brand new when they put it in. Please let me know what I can do? I do beleive there are more dishwashers out there that are unsafe.

My Vino View Wine Enthusiast refrigerator is leaking, and growing mold on my wine bottles. When i notified the company for the 2nd time, they informed me my unit was defective and they have been having issues with this make and model, but "not enough" to do a recall. They are well aware their product is defective but they are not doing anything for the consumers who purchased this item.
Husband put on self cleaning oven feature of our GE double wall oven and the glass exploded.

The exterior glass panel on our oven door spontaneously exploded outward sending glass shards spraying 3 feet across our kitchen. The oven was not being used at the time and hadn't been used at all that day so it was completely cool to the touch.

08/19/2011-Today I was making dinner and my Left Front Burner on my Frigidaire Smoothtop range malfunctioned. I Boiled potatoes on High in a pot that fit the burner, then simmered the potatoes on 2 or 3. When I shut the burner OFF and removed the pot from the burner it continued to Glow RED and produce massive amounts of heat. The burner continued in this state for about 30 - 45 seconds. I toggled the knob between low and off a few times and it shut down.

I understand a recall has been issued on my Samsung top load washer. I have also been experiencing same reported incidences of unusually high agitation where it seems as though the top will "blow off". Please advise of next step to repair or replace.

The consumer stated that he was using the dishwasher and it had been on for approximately 1 hour and a half. The consumer stated that he heard a noise and started to smell an electrical burning odor. The consumer stated that his wife went into the kitchen and saw smoke being emitted from the upper right hand corner of the door. The consumer stated that immediately turned off the break and the dishwasher stopped emitting the smoke within 30 seconds. The consumer stated that he could not see any visible damages on the dishwasher. The consumer stated that there were no damages to his home structure aside from the bad burnt odor. The consumer stated that no one was injured. The consumer stated that he contacted the manufacturer and they asked him to contact them back because there system was down. The consumer stated that this product should be investigated do to the fire hazard it poses to the consumer.

The stovetop burners stay on, even after they are turned off at the controls. Then, my daughter who has a disability, went later to use the range and the burners were still unexpectedly very hot. She could have been badly burned or had her clothes catch fire. When I spoke with a GE customer service rep, they said that this could be caused by the stovetop not being cleaned enough, but such a weakness in the design seems very hazardous because they should expect that a stovetop will sometimes have food spills on it.

Purchased KitchenAid, convection, vented hood microwave near beginning of 2013. We were in the process of using the timer which had about 15 minutes left on a 1 hour setting. We were not touching the microwave when the fans began to blow fiercely. Opening the door had no impact on the unit and it was getting dangerously hot and quickly. We killed the power supply by disengaging the breaker within a minute of when the unit started itself. Once the unit cooled, we were able to unplug the cord from the wall socket and inspect the unit. The convection oven must have been running un-commanded. The glass turntable has black markings in it and the plastic at the base is now warped. I believe the space inside the microwave is damaged as well, but this is just speculation at this point. I am confident that if we had not been at home and readily in the area to stop the power feed to the unit then there would have been a fire or an explosion from the microwave starting on its own.

The consumer stated that she turned on the oven on pre-heat at she opened the door and placed her food in the oven. The consumer stated that within seconds after closing the door the oven glass door exploded. The consumer stated that the glass door exploded outwards shattering all over her kitchen. The consumer stated that the oven was approximately at 200 degrees, it had not reached the 350 degrees she had set it for. The consumer stated that she immediately turned off the range. The consumer stated that she was not using the burners of the range; she was only using the oven. The consumer stated that the outer glass was the only one that exploded; the inner glass was still intact. She stated that the glass reached as far as 3’ away from the range. The consumer stated that no one was injured and there were no damages to her home structure. The consumer stated that she contacted the retailer and they set up an appointment for a technician to service the range on 07/25/2013. The consumer stated that she will be contacting the manufacturer to file a report. The consumer stated that she believed that this product should be investigated due to the laceration hazard that it poses to consumers.

The product is a Midea U-Shaped Window Air Conditioner that suffers from the critical drainage failure detailed in CPSC Recall Notice #25-241. Water pools heavily in the base pan and fails to drain, creating an active, trapped mold hazard inside my apartment unit. Compounding this issue, the unit has suffered a total mechanical failure, displaying the EC 07 error code (outdoor fan speed/compressor failure). Because I live in an apartment building with stairs, this heavy, mold-retaining appliance is a physical and biological hazard trapped in my living space. Local handymen refuse to touch or transport the unit due to the active mold growth and complex U-shaped structural frame. The manufacturer, Midea, has refused to assist with the physical removal or installation of a safe alternative, trying instead to force an inadequate prorated cash offer that does not cover the cost of hazardous product extraction.

The oven door shattered while I was cooking on the stove top. The oven was not on at the time, there was no impact to the oven door. This oven, a Frigidaire, model # FFEF3054TS 30" is only 2 years old

The consumer indicates that she turned her dishwasher on and, fifteen minutes later when she went into the kitchen, realized that her floor was covered in water. The consumer turned off and unplugged the unit. The following day, the consumer's son and husband looked behind it to see if there were any leaking hoses and there were none. The consumer's son looked inside the unit, removed its rack, and saw that the heating element was burnt. The consumer contacted the Manufacturer and explained the situation; the representative she spoke to informed her that because the unit is no longer under warranty nor is it recalled that they could not assist her free of charge. The consumer states that the unit is used four to five times weekly. The consumer plans on keeping her dishwasher for at least the next thirty days in case an investigation ensues.

My wife was doing routine cleaning of our LG refrigerator. She removed the bottom glass shelf and wiped it with a cool, damp cloth, which had been done before. Moments later the glass exploded into small pieces and sent small pieces flying as far as 10-12ft throughout the area. Injuries were minimal, only a minor scratch when someone stepped on a piece. However, glass was everywhere and we consider it a close call that no additional injuries were incurred. We searched around the internet and found several message boards where this exact situation had occurred on many occasions with other people. Regardless of what LG may claim, there is no way this glass is in accordance with safety standards for shattering glass, etc.
My house caught on fire and we lost everything. We have video footage and picture of where the fire started and that the deep freeze was the cause of my fire.

Frigidaire Induction Range burners turn on by themselves. All 4 burners turn on and get extremely hot, then the range beeps and the burners turned off, only to turn back on after a minute or so. This happened repeatedly and fill the house with a smell of burning plastic. I turned off the breaker for 15 minutes and within an hour it happened again, so we are leaving the breaker off and trying to work with the warranty service (through Home Depot) to have the unit replaced, but so far they have not been helpful. A technician came out to diagnose the range and did not find any issues and said that the Frigidaire service line spokesperson said he had never heard of this happening before, which seems hard to believe as you can find a lot of posts online about the same thing happening to others. I am continuing to try to work with the warranty service to get this replaced or some sort of compensation for a different range.
GE Model JVM1540DM5WW spacemaker microwave oven, installed in 2013. Plastic from the inside ceiling of microwave is literally melting and dropping balls of plastic into our food!

LG Studio 6.3 cu. ft. Electric Single Oven Slide-in-range with ProBake Convection has knobs on front of oven that are easily turned on or turned when on, by children, pets or just while cooking at stove. Have had couple episodes where this happened and melted plastic/silicone utensils and of handles. Had worst episode when came on unknowingly, and plastic knob covers were sitting on stove along with some packets of cocoa mix, causing a lot of smoke in home.

The knobs of my gas range have broken. I have switched them around to be able to use the most used burners but they all have broken now. Now I have to turn the burners off without the knobs. When I was using the stovetop the other night, I thought I had turned off a burner but it remained on, at a very low setting. Had I not turned off the room lights immediately after, I would not have noticed it on and would have left the burner on indefinitely. LG will replace defective knobs for other models but refuses to replace for my model, LRG39355st. They gave me a parts distributor that quoted $63 per knob (with 5 knobs, that would be over $300, might as well buy a new range that works). I cannot afford either at this point so I will have to do without a stovetop for now.
The refrigerator center panel heats up to extreme temperatures. Bother Freezer and Fridge door also get very hot. The condenser fan stops working and makes a strange noise.

I have a KitchenAid refrigerator/freezer with an ice and water dispenser built into the door. About two years ago the ice and water dispenser stopped working. I then called the authorized KitchenAid repair service. The responding repair technician was able to fix the problem which had to do with wiring in the door. Recently, the same problem occurred and I again called the authorized service. The technician informed me that the problem is a recurrence of the original problem, namely, the same wires are frayed and broken and now they cannot be repaired. My concern is that frayed and broken electrical wires in a refrigerator/freezer may be a dangerous condition perhaps leading to electrical shock or worse.

I have a fairly new (2019) Samsung refrigerator with French doors (model #RF23HCED8SR/AA). I noticed that the temperature inside did not match the 34 degrees F shown on the display. Food was not keeping well and spoiling as I was not aware that the temp was inaccurate until I checked the temperature using my own kitchen thermometer. Water was accumulating in and below the crisper drawers which added humidity to the fridge. I have had more stomach problems over the past few months and have to be careful to check inside containers for mold. I called Samsung today for service and also have a problem with the ice maker not working and freezing the drawer making it impossible to pull out. I had to be careful not to hurt myself trying to remove the drawer since it was stuck and located near the fridge door.

On August 18, 2019 my Rheem XE50M12EC55U1 electric water heater purchased in July 2018 at Home Depot tripped the circuit breaker. On inspection, the wires inside had completely melted and caught fire. I have spent the past two weeks trimming and re-connecting the wiring, but after about a week of use the wires melt again. I have a 30 di-pole breaker installed with 10 gauge wire, which should provide enough capacity to power the 5500 amp unit. It is simply unsafe, and it appears Rheem has not corrected the issues that caused the XE50M12EC55U0 recall on May 26, 2016.
Washing a load of clothes. I smelled smoke and found that the washer was emitting smoke (a noxious, plastic smoke).

Over the past five months we have had a persistent problem with the Rheem water heater's pilot light going out. As the enclosed chronology clearly indicates, your defective product caused us major inconveniences, and more importantly, the defect exposed us to a potentially dangerous situation. On Christmas Eve, the City of Palo Alto Utilities Department field service representative discovered the heater had a faulty ignition and turned off the gas due to the hazardous condition it presented. Rheem customer representatives had assured us the problem of the pilot light's frequently going out would be resolved by the replacement parts they sent us. When the pilot light problems continued even after installation of the replacement parts, your last customer representative said the problem may be with the utilities company and that we should ask the City to pressure test the gas flow. It was as if he absolved Rheem of any responsibility because all possible parts had already been replaced. As the chronology clearly shows, this was not the case. Once the City of Palo Alto turned off the gas to the water heater, I lost all faith in Rheem and had the water heater removed even though it still possesses a long-term warranty. Assuring the safety of my family pre-empts any warranty. Since the replacement parts did not resolve the problem and continued to put us at risk, I am demanding reimbursement of $453 that I paid to have parts installed in attempting to fix the inherently defective water heater. [REDACTED]

I have a GE dishwasher that was purchased approximately 3 years ago. I was told by the product support specialist that this model was first manufactured in 2019. This dishwasher had a wheel for the lower rack that kept popping off. We just popped it back on. We then realized it wasn't rolling properly. I assumed maybe the fact that it was warped (and now I know, melted) is why the wheel kept popping off. Then, the other night, I woke up a little after midnight to the smell of burning plastic. We immediately stopped the dishwasher, found that that same roller somehow ended up on the element and was melting. We pulled the melted plastic piece off of the element. We also had to open up windows to air out the house, closed the bedroom doors to stop more fumes from entering into our rooms, and the kids' rooms. The fumes smelled very toxic! I contacted the manufacturer as I didn't see any recalls on this particular product, but I've seen them for dishwashers in general. I was told we should order a new roller piece and have a new element installed.
My samsung washer, has black mold and when I wash my clothes they smell like mold regardless of how I clean it still keep coming back. Doing this to hopefully get this resolved.
LG MICROWAVE MODEL # MS1440ACS.CWHELGA, SERIAL# 103TALB00608, purchased [REDACTED] is intermittantly starting on its own when the door is closed.

Frigidaire Gallery Air conditioner FGRC1044T1 grew mold inside. My cats now have respiratory infections and asthma. I noticed the mold at the end of last summer, but not sure if it was growing before that.

Top water supply hose to Frigidaire FDB2410 is about 1 inch too short. After about a year or two it wiggled itself free of the clamp and flooded the area beneath the dishwasher and tripped the GFCI breaker on the box under the sink. Had to rewire the area given the flood and paid for a service call to verify that the design is defective.

While a Bosch 24-Inch Smart Compact Front Load Washer (Model WAW285H2UC) was running a normal wash cycle, the front door blew out unexpectedly. A 70-year-old woman was in close proximity at the time. She was not injured, but the force of the door failure could have caused serious harm. The washer was purchased in June 2022 and was being used normally with no modifications. The product has a dangerous defect that allowed the pressurized door to detach mid-cycle.
Control panel on water [heater] caught fire

There is mold in the product. I called the help line and opened a case number- when they reviewed the details they said Yes it is part of the recall, but the recall people will not honor it even though this unit if purchased before 2025 is known to have issues with mold. There is mold clearly in the unit.

Husband was sitting at table and heard noises, then smelled terrible plastic/electrical smoke coming from the dishwasher. Immediately stopped it but couldnt find anything. Tirned off electricity and stayed around until we were sure there was no active fire. Researched it the next day , thought it was a motor, but found the door panel electrical box and wires black and melted .. even the fiberglass melted! So glad we were inside the house to catch it! We have never had work done on the door, but the electrical box was NOT screwed on like the soap dispenser, etc. instead it was secured with black tape which disintegrated with age!!! Our house could have burned down because of poor quality manufacturing!!!

I own the Whirlpool Microwave-Hood combo with Model #WMH53520cs - 6 with a manufactured date of September 2016. A piece of the plastic within the microwave began dripping slowly and eventually, the piece of plastic that was hanging fell to the floor of the microwave. This has created a hole in the ceiling of the microwave. This model has a recall but the serial # I have is not included in a preexisting recall. I am not able to find a resource to let me know if the device is safe to continue being used. There is no metal inside of the unit to have caused this.

During normal cycle, my 18 month old Whirlpool dishwasher (GU2275XTVB1) began emitting a strong burning plastic smell. I checked for any items that may have fallen and were burning down below, but nothing was there. It continued running and I began opening windows and turning on fans, still thinking it was just the large amount of plastic ware that I had in the washer. I moved my two small children upstairs away from the terrible smell, only to find it had already spread throughout our home. The smell became overwhelming and I immediately went to turn off the dishwasher, only to find that it had already tripped my circuit breaker. My husband pulled it out and turned it upside down to find severely charred wiring underneath and the metal parts were charcoal black. I'm so thankful that our circuit breaker tripped and that we didn't start it in the early morning when my husband leaves for work like we normally do. I have lost faith in Whirlpool products due to this scary incident that left us all coughing and trying to air out the house. After reading other similar stories, I strongly believe this should be recalled before people are actually killed by these faulty dishwashers.
